pr_title: Fix duplicate route detection of actions with route parameters
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/49777

A previous fix handled the situation where `[action]` replacement tokens in a route could cause false positives. Using a replacement token for `[action]` is recommended by our docs, but `{action}` can do the same thing.

This PR fixes `{action}` route tokens in the route analyzer.

Example:
```cs
[Route("api/[controller]")]
[ApiController]
public class MyController : ControllerBase
{
    [HttpGet("{action}")]
    public IActionResult GetTime() => Ok(DateTime.Now.ToString("HH:mm:ss"));
    
    [HttpGet("{action}")]
    public IActionResult GetDate() => Ok(DateTime.Now.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd"));
}
```

issue_context.title: ASP0023 Ambiguous route warning when targeting .NET 8 and using token [action] or [controller] in [Http*] or [Route] attributes
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

When targeting .NET 8 preview 6 and using token [action] or [controller] in [Http*] or [Route] attributes on a controller method, an ASP0023 warning is emitted which is a new behaviour that wasn't observed in .NET 7.

If you ignore the warnings, the code will run and the endpoints can be called and return the expected responses for their respective verbs.

### Expected Behavior

No warning generated

### Steps To Reproduce

```
var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
builder.Services.AddControllers();

var app = builder.Build();
app.MapControllers();
app.Run();

[Route("api/[controller]")]
[ApiController]
public class MyController : ControllerBase
{
    [HttpGet("[action]")]
    public IActionResult GetTime() => Ok(DateTime.Now.ToString("HH:mm:ss"));
    
    [HttpGet("[action]")]
    public IActionResult GetDate() => Ok(DateTime.Now.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd"));
}
```

### Exceptions (if any)

No response

### .NET Version

8.0.100-preview.6.23330.14

Edited: My example was actually incorrect, the analyzer only identifies matches within the _same_ controller. I've updated the comment to be more accurate, but the info I've added isn't much beyond the initial report.

> The behavior is the same regardless of where the `[action]` part of the route is set. Example below errors as well
> 
> ``` csharp
> [Route("api/[controller]/[action]")]
> [ApiController]
> public class Controller1 : ControllerBase
> {
>     [HttpGet("{id:int}")]
>     public IActionResult GetMethod1(int id) => Ok();
>    
>     [HttpGet("{id:int}")]
>     public IActionResult GetMethod2(int id) => Ok();

> ```

Analyzer was introduced in PR https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/45915.
@JamesNK is there chance analyzer behavior will be fixed on .net 8 release?
If there's a bug in the analyzer and it's patched in servicing, it's not going to make it into the 8.0.0 release at this point.

> Analyzer was introduced in PR #45915. @JamesNK is there chance analyzer behavior will be fixed on .net 8 release?

No, .NET 8 is locked down for only urgent fixes right now. This is a bug but not a critical one. However, it can be fixed in 8.0.x release later this year or early next year.

I suggest you disable the analyzer in the project file with `<NoWarn>ASP0023</NoWarn>`:

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <NoWarn>ASP0023</NoWarn>
  </PropertyGroup>

</Project>
```

Or in code:

```cs
    [Route("api/[controller]/[action]")]
    [ApiController]
    public class Controller1 : ControllerBase
    {
#pragma warning disable ASP0023 // Route conflict detected between controller actions
        [HttpGet("{id:int}")]
        public IActionResult GetMethod1(int id) => Ok();

        [HttpGet("{id:int}")]
        public IActionResult GetMethod2(int id) => Ok();
#pragma warning restore ASP0023 // Route conflict detected between controller actions
    }
```

And reenable when the analyzer is fixed.

After upgrading VS to 17.8.4 (which is how I'm currently getting my .NET 8 SDK) the .NET SDK updated to 8.0.101 and I no longer receive the warnings.

We're still getting the warnings in 8.0.1. For a minimal repro, I created a new project using the "ASP.NET Core Web API" template with "Use controllers" checked. It generated a `WeatherForecastController`. and I changed it to look like this:

``` C#
namespace WebApplication2.Controllers;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

[ApiController]
[Route("[controller]")]
public class WeatherForecastController : ControllerBase
{
    private static readonly string[] Summaries = new[]
    {
        "Freezing", "Bracing", "Chilly", "Cool", "Mild", "Warm", "Balmy", "Hot", "Sweltering", "Scorching"
    };

    [HttpGet]
    [Route("{action}")]
    public IEnumerable<WeatherForecast> GetWeatherForecast()
    {
        return Enumerable.Range(1, 5).Select(index => new WeatherForecast
        {
            Date = DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.Now.AddDays(index)),
            TemperatureC = Random.Shared.Next(-20, 55),
            Summary = Summaries[Random.Shared.Next(Summaries.Length)]
        })
        .ToArray();
    }

    [HttpGet]
    [Route("{action}")]
    public IEnumerable<string> GetSummaries() => Summaries;
}
```

The ASP0023 analyzer highlights both `[Route("{action}")]` lines. When I run the project, Swagger throws an exception because it can't handle two HttpGets:

``` stacktrace
Swashbuckle.AspNetCore.SwaggerGen.SwaggerGeneratorException
  HResult=0x80131500
  Message=Conflicting method/path combination "GET WeatherForecast/{action}" for actions - WebApplication3.Controllers.WeatherForecastController.Get (WebApplication3),WebApplication3.Controllers.WeatherForecastController.GetSummaries (WebApplication3). Actions require a unique method/path combination for Swagger/OpenAPI 3.0. Use ConflictingActionsResolver as a workaround
  Source=Swashbuckle.AspNetCore.SwaggerGen
  StackTrace:
   at Swashbuckle.AspNetCore.SwaggerGen.SwaggerGenerator.GenerateOperations(IEnumerable`1 apiDescriptions, SchemaRepository schemaRepository)
   at Swashbuckle.AspNetCore.SwaggerGen.SwaggerGenerator.GeneratePaths(IEnumerable`1 apiDescriptions, SchemaRepository schemaRepository)
   at Swashbuckle.AspNetCore.SwaggerGen.SwaggerGenerator.GetSwaggerDocumentWithoutFilters(String documentName, String host, String basePath)
   at Swashbuckle.AspNetCore.SwaggerGen.SwaggerGenerator.<GetSwaggerAsync>d__6.MoveNext()
   at Swashbuckle.AspNetCore.Swagger.SwaggerMiddleware.<Invoke>d__4.MoveNext()
```

However, both routes work just fine when invoked directly. Putting `https://localhost:7216/WeatherForecast/GetSummaries` in a browser window returns:
``` json
["Freezing","Bracing","Chilly","Cool","Mild","Warm","Balmy","Hot","Sweltering","Scorching"]
```

Putting `https://localhost:7216/WeatherForecast/GetWeatherForecast` in browser window returns:
``` json
[{"date":"2024-01-12","temperatureC":16,"temperatureF":60,"summary":"Scorching"},{"date":"2024-01-13","temperatureC":12,"temperatureF":53,"summary":"Bracing"},{"date":"2024-01-14","temperatureC":22,"temperatureF":71,"summary":"Mild"},{"date":"2024-01-15","temperatureC":32,"temperatureF":89,"summary":"Balmy"},{"date":"2024-01-16","temperatureC":41,"temperatureF":105,"summary":"Scorching"}]
```

The routes are not ambiguous given how the `{action}` token is interpreted in a [route template](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/routing?view=aspnetcore-8.0#route-templates), so I don't think ASP0023 should complain about them. At a minimum, it seems like a rule with too many false positives and not enough documentation to explain what it's really trying to warn about. Maybe, it's saying "Swagger doesn't support this." But it's not reporting _ambiguous_ routes in these cases. 

The rule's error message's first sentence is incorrect given how route templates are processed.

``` text
Route '{action}' conflicts with another action route. An HTTP request that matches multiple routes results in an ambiguous match error. Fix the conflict by changing the route's pattern, HTTP method, or route constraints.
```

The [rule's documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/diagnostics/asp0023?view=aspnetcore-8.0) doesn't provide any useful information other than a minimal restatement of that error message.

Note that if I remove the `[Route("{action}")]` attributes, then neither API will work because an HTTP GET request is ambiguous. But with the attributes present, the routes are not ambiguous.

This minimal repro case is a simplified, contrived example of my old, real-world project where I'm seeing a bunch of ASP0023 errors. It has a few controllers that have multiple HttpGet and HttpPut methods tagged with `[Route("{action}")]`, and the routes are _not_ ambiguous. They work fine now and have for years. So, maybe the documentation for ASP0023 needs to say it's ok to suppress this rule if your controllers intentionally distinguish HTTP actions by using the `{action}` route template instead of just saying, "Do not suppress a warning from this rule."

Curly-braced tokens are used for passing parameters from url to handler.
There is nice post about it
https://dotnettutorials.net/lesson/model-binding-using-fromroute-in-asp-net-core-mvc/

I've spent more time researching this today, and Microsoft's routing docs are kind of a mess about it. [This section](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/mvc/controllers/routing?view=aspnetcore-8.0#token-replacement-in-route-templates-controller-action-area) says:

> For convenience, attribute routes support token replacement by enclosing a token in square-brackets ([, ]). The tokens [action], [area], and [controller] are replaced with the values of the action name, area name, and controller name from the action where the route is defined:

Then [further down on that same page](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/mvc/controllers/routing?view=aspnetcore-8.0#specifying-attribute-route-optional-parameters-default-values-and-constraints), it says:

> Attribute routes support the same inline syntax as conventional routes to specify optional parameters, default values, and constraints.

Then it links to a [Route Template Reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/routing?view=aspnetcore-8.0#route-template-reference) page, which uses `{action}` six times and never uses `[action]`.

The fact that attribute route processing supports `{action}` at runtime, but Swagger and the ASP0023 rule don't support it seems very inconsistent. I can't find a Microsoft-documented reason for it. Attribute routing is documented to support two syntaxes for token replacements (`{}` and `[]`), but these external tools don't follow the same convention.

I increased the severity of the [ASP0018](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/diagnostics/asp0018) "Unused route parameter" rule to Error, so it flagged the `{action}` parameter as unused and gave a compile error. Then I fixed all those places to use `[action]`. Now the rules work together to prevent us from using the non-preferred syntax in the future.

I think we can make the analyzer special case `{action}`.

Using `[action]` token replacement is much more common, but a `{action}` parameter works with routing, so the analyzer should handle it without false positives.

Using `{action}` instead of `[action]` still results in the same warning as before.

Does this affect the actual behavior of anything or is it just an analyzer? Still seeing an issue using either as of today (2024-01-15)

This seems like a poorly written validation: the methodes  with different names but marked with the same {action} (or [action] route template clearly do not represent the same endpoint: there is no ambiguity during routing.

BTW, the problem is still present in the latest SDK and version of VS (8.0.101/17.8.5)

review_comments: Should we add a test that covers one route using `[action]` and another using `{action}`?
What kind of sick person would do that? I love it.

I looked at this and the test isn't necessary. `HttpGet("[action]")` and `HttpGet("{action}")` aren't flagged as ambiguous because the routes are different.

Technically they should be ambiguous if on two actions of the same name, but realistically no one will ever do this. The analyzer will stick with the pattern of being conservative about what it reports and not handle this situation.
